# REAL mail pcap — provenance (NOT synthetic)

File: `lab/pcaps/real-mail-starttls-587.pcap` (3996 bytes, 28 packets)
Generator: `lab/scripts/real_mail_capture.py` (re-run to reproduce; loopback capture
is blocked in this sandbox — `dumpcap: Permission denied` — so L2–L4 framing
is reconstructed with scapy; see below for exactly what is real).

## What is REAL (generated by live software, not knobs)
- SMTP dialogue over a real TCP socket to a real SMTP server implementation:
  `220 mail.lab.local ESMTP Postfix 3.9.0`, `EHLO`, `250-STARTTLS`
  advertisement, `STARTTLS`, `220 2.0.0 Ready to start TLS`.
- TLS handshake bytes from a REAL OpenSSL handshake (`ssl.MemoryBIO` pair,
  same parameters as the live socket session): ClientHello / ServerHello /
  Certificate (real DER of `lab/certs/rsa2048.crt`, CN=mail.lab.local,
  issuer CN=lab.local, valid Aug–Nov 2026) / Finished.
- Negotiated session (verified on the live socket): TLS 1.2,
  `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`.
- Post-handshake ApplicationData: real AES-GCM ciphertext (`MAIL FROM`
  encrypted by OpenSSL, decrypted back to prove it).
- tshark dissects it independently: SMTP lines + `tls.handshake.ciphersuite
  0xc030`, version 0x0303.

## What is RECONSTRUCTED (label honestly)
- Ether/IP/TCP headers + seq/ack numbers (framed with scapy; endpoints
  127.0.0.11:54330 → 127.0.0.12:587). Payload bytes untouched.

## Verified pipeline result (2026-09-09, PYTHONHASHSEED=0)
- Reassembler: coverage 1.0, `starttls_detected=True`,
  `starttls_advertised=True`, no injection, `tshark_used=True`.
- Parser: TLS1.2, strong AEAD cipher, FS true, handshake success, JA4 ok.
- Verdict (`_real_pipeline_for_bytes`): smtp / upgrade → risk 13 Medium,
  posture 87. Findings: TLS-1.2-outdated (Medium) + 6 Info
  (incl. KeyUsage/EKU — lab cert is minimal).
- Known gap: full chain-validation finding did not fire on this flow
  (validator needs Certificate DER via the parse path) — follow-up, do not
  claim chain-validated on this pcap.
